title: Control plane decision DSL — examples & notes
content:
Purpose:
This note collects concrete examples and executable patterns for a compact control-plane DSL to express multi-region request steering. The goal: let product/platform engineers declare intent (SLO priorities, cost caps, region preferences) and have the routing layer compile that into deterministic decision trees and fallbacks.

Context and motivation:
- Current routing policies are a mix of hard-coded heuristics and config blobs. Hard to reason about combined constraints (latency vs cost vs reliability).
- Want a small, testable language that:
  * expresses weights and hard constraints,
  * compiles to readable decision trees for audit and debugging,
  * can be evaluated cheaply in the control plane and emitted as policy fingerprints to edge routers.

Design goals (practical):
1) Priority-first semantics: allow teams to specify a lexicographic ordering — e.g., first satisfy latency SLO, then minimize cost under that constraint.
2) Constraints + objective: support boolean constraints (region in EU), numeric caps (max-cost-per-1000=5.0), and objectives (minimize-p99-latency).
3) Deterministic fallbacks: explicit fallback chains so behavior during degraded capacity is predictable.
4) Explainability: generated decision tree nodes must include which constraint produced the branch.
5) Small surface area: language should be ~10 constructs (predicates, weights, objectives, fallbacks, annotations).

Quick grammar sketch (informal):
- policy ::= policy <name> { attributes* rules* }
- attributes ::= priority: <list-of-keys> | cost_cap: <float> | regions: <list> | annotation: <string>
- rule ::= when <predicate> then <action> [fallback <action>]
- predicate ::= metric(operator,value) | region(in|not_in, list) | model(family) | true
- action ::= route_to(group) | sample(route,percent) | degrade(model_variant) | deny

Example 1 — latency-first, cost-aware routing (product features):
policy low-latency-features {
  priority: [latency_p95, reliability]
  cost_cap: 7.5   # $ per 1000 tokens (soft)
  regions: [us-west, us-east, eu-west]

  # Fast path: local GPU pool with KV cache hit and healthy nodes
  when region(in, caller_region) and cache(hit) and pool(healthy) then route_to(local-hot) fallback route_to(local-warm)

  # If cache miss or local overloaded, prefer regional dedicated if latency OK
  when latency_estimate(p95) < 120 and pool(dedicated,available) then route_to(regional-dedicated) fallback route_to(shared-lowcost)

  # As last resort, route to lowest-latency cross-region variant within cost cap
  when cost_estimate(1000tokens) <= cost_cap then route_to(cross-region-optimized) fallback deny
}
Notes on Example 1:
- Each "when" compiles into a subtree that checks predicates in order.
- cost_estimate is evaluated from short profiles; control plane caches recent estimates.
- fallback actions annotated into the generated tree so runtime logs can show fallback reason.

Example 2 — reliability-first for enterprise customer (hard constraints):
policy enterprise-reliable {
  priority: [reliability, latency]
  regions: [eu-west, us-central]
  annotation: "Customer XYZ: GDPR + 4 9s availability SLA"

  when service_health(cluster) >= 99.99 and region(in, eu-west) then route_to(enterprise-pool) fallback route_to(enterprise-failover)
  when true then deny  # explicit deny if no enterprise pools available (protects data locality + SLA)
}
Key differences here: team explicitly requires deny instead of falling back to shared pools.

Compiling to decision trees (example representation):
- Node: CHECK service_health(cluster) >= 99.99 -> TRUE branch: CHECK region(in, eu-west) -> TRUE: ACTION route_to(enterprise-pool)
- Each node contains metadata: source-policy, source-line, config-hash.

Heuristics / evaluation ordering patterns:
- Short-circuit: cheap predicates (region, cache_hit) first; expensive preds (latency_estimate via model) later.
- Probabilistic sampling: include sample(route,10%) nodes to send small fraction to candidate regions/variants for continuous eval.
- Hysteresis: require N consecutive failures before failing over to avoid oscillation. Attach a TTL to branches.

Small example of hysteresis annotation:
when pool(healthy) < 95 then route_to(shared-warm) fallback route_to(shared-lowcost) // hysteresis: require 3/5 failures, cooldown 30s

Operational considerations:
- Policy validation: static checks (cost_cap sanity, region mismatch with customer constraints).
- Simulation harness: control-plane should be able to run policy against traffic traces to produce expected routes and cost/latency distributions. Store the trace id in policy metadata.
- Telemetry: every routed request should include policy-id and branch-path for downstream analytics (cost attribution, SLO reconciliation).
- Rollouts: policy actors should be versioned and rollout via the same rollout subsystem as model versions (canary -> a/b -> global).

Decision-tree pruning and complexity management:
- Limit depth by rewriting rules: merge identical leaf actions, hoist common predicates.
- Reject policies that expand beyond X nodes (configurable) unless explicitly marked as high-complexity and reviewed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Canonical cost model: we need an internal API that maps model variant + region + sequence_length_distribution to expected $/1k. Who owns this? (cc: finance)
- How to express soft vs hard objectives in DSL more explicitly (enum vs numeric slack)?
- Persistence model: store policy compiled tree + source DSL. Plan: keep both to allow round-trip editing.
- Debug UX: create a UI to show policy evaluation for a synthetic request (input: region, token_count, cache_hit).

Quick simulation snapshot (run on sample t-shirt traces):
- Policy low-latency-features (traffic=100k req/day):
  * expected p95 latency: 98 ms; expected cost: $5.9 / 1k tokens.
  * with cost_cap lowered to 4.0 -> p95 increases to 170 ms, more cross-region fallbacks.
- Enterprise-reliable: denies ~0.002% of requests in the trace (mostly due to strict deny rule), investigate whether deny spikes correlate with regional deploys.

Auditability and compliance notes:
- Every policy change should create a deployment record with diff and signer. For enterprise policies with deny rules, require an approval step.
- Keep an immutable log of compiled-trees for forensics (indexed by policy-hash and time).

Examples of real-world policy snippets to copy/paste (for internal teams):
# prefer low-cost but only if p99 < 250ms
policy cost-conscious {
  priority: [cost, latency_p99]
  cost_cap: 3.5
  when latency_estimate(p99) < 250 and pool(shared,available) then route_to(shared-lowcost) fallback route_to(shared-warm)
  when true then route_to(regional-dedicated)
}

# sample 5% of traffic to a new quantized model variant for quality checks
policy experiment-quant-5pct {
  priority: [safety, latency]
  when true then sample(new-quant,5%) fallback route_to(current)
}

Related tickets / follow-up actions:
- JIRA-PLAT-987: canonical cost model owner (assign to Finance Eng)
- PR #482 (control-plane): add predicate cost_estimate and sample builtin
- UX: spike to render policy trees in the console (owners: devexp)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft; looking for feedback on: predicate primitives, how to express soft constraints, and whether to include a richer expression language vs keeping it intentionally small.
- If we agree on the shape, follow-up work: implement parser, unit test harness, and simulation runner.

Author: Aisha Kapoor (platform-engineering)
